server/stores/connector-instance-store.j.reason: D8 (fix-enroll-connector-instance-pk-collision): a live counterexample proved connector_instances.upsert's INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(owner, connector, source_kind, source_binding_key) is not resilient to a PRIMARY KEY collision against a legacy row for the SAME logical binding whose source_binding_key was computed under an OLDER, larger sourceBinding shape (embedding per-enrollment device_id/source_instance_id) that predates deviceExporterSourceBindingIdentity's stable {kind, local_binding_name}-only shape. That legacy row's id predates makeConnectorInstanceId and coincides with what today's formula computes for this same binding under its current key. Reaching the INSERT already proves the named ON CONFLICT target did not match this binding under its CURRENT key, so a 23505 here means either (a) the colliding row is this same binding under a legacy key (a migration, not a collision), or (b) it is a genuinely unrelated row (must fail closed). Both backends (Postgres try/catch; SQLite equivalent catching SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_PRIMARYKEY) now look up the colliding row and migrate it in place -- UPDATE its source_binding_key/source_binding_json to the current shape and return its SAME connector_instance_id -- ONLY when isSameLogicalBindingUnderLegacyKey proves it (same owner/connector/source_kind, and the local_binding_name embedded in its OWN stored source_binding_json matches); any other collision re-throws the raw 23505 unmodified. Proven load-bearing by a mutation test: reverting the migration logic makes the Postgres D8 regression (device-enroll-postgres-admission-decoupling.test.js) fail deterministically 3/3 runs with the exact live 503 enrollment_identity_conflict symptom; a SQLite unit test (connector-instance-store.test.js) additionally proves the fail-closed path for an unrelated colliding row.

lib/postgres-spine.js.reason: mergeEventRows fix for a silent data-loss bug (distinct rows sharing a null/duplicate event_seq collapsed onto the same dedup key). The fix needs a two-key (event_seq, event_id) comparator, which Biome's cognitive-complexity scoring counts as added mass even when extracted into its own named function (compareEventRowOrder) — tried extraction first; it did not reduce the file-level score. Correctness over a lower number here.

lib/spine.ts.reason: loadEventsForSummaries batches the summary-hydration N+1 (one query per correlation id -> one query for the whole page) via a ROW_NUMBER()-partitioned fetch plus a per-id grouping pass (building the id->rows Map, iterating placeholders, hydrating rows). That control flow — not the SQL string literal itself — is what Biome's cognitive-complexity scoring counts as added mass; the SQL text's explicit `(event_seq IS NULL), event_seq, event_id` ordering is necessary because summarizeEvents derives status/source/browser-surface state from array position (first/last event, reverse scans), so the grouped rows must arrive in a caller-guaranteed total order rather than relying on the window function's undocumented partition-membership-only guarantee. This mass was already present at PR #368's head without a justification entry; adding one here rather than reducing it further, since the batching mechanism and its ordering contract are load-bearing correctness, not incidental style.

server/connector-manifest-validation.ts.reason: Port of main's external-tool detection hardening (security fix e6e96933b) + owner-cancel/recovery surfaces from #199/#190 reconciliation; behavior required by main's test contract. Queued for decomposition in the Phase-1 drain.

server/db.js.reason: The SQLite migration must inventory recognized enum shapes, preserve dependent objects, rebuild atomically, and fail closed before committing a foreign_key_check. These independent persistence safety branches are necessary to avoid lossy migration of historical schemas.

server/postgres-storage.js.reason: The PostgreSQL migration serializes public legacy bootstraps before catalog discovery with bounded pg_try_advisory_lock polling, distinguishes exact direct legacy/current checks from unrelated compound checks, and performs transactional rollback. The polling/lock classification and fail-closed branches are required to avoid broad constraint deletion, concurrent startup failure, or concurrent-index deadlock.

server/stores/connector-detail-gap-store.reason: The SQLite and Postgres implementations must each make the same run-and-lease-owned compare-and-set transitions for claim, explicit attempt, recovery, re-deferral, release, and expired-lease reclaim. The branches preserve the distinction between an untouched issuance and a real provider attempt across durable backend dialects; collapsing them behind a shallow helper would hide the SQL ownership predicates that prevent re-serve races.

server/routes/ref-device-exporters.ts.reason: decouple-device-enrollment-from-ingest-writer-admission adds the idempotent re-enroll path (handleIdempotentReEnroll) that recovers a one-time device credential lost to a transport failure: it must enforce four independent safeguards (unexpired code, same bound device, device-not-revoked, same binding) before atomically rotating the credential, emit an audit receipt, and reject every other consumed-code replay — plus a typed-503 backpressure mapping (respondEnrollError). The enroll handler itself was decomposed first (performFirstEnrollment, handleIdempotentReEnroll, respondEnrollError all extracted, each within the per-function complexity budget); the residual file-level mass is the four safeguard branches, which are load-bearing correctness for a live credential-loss fix, not incidental style. D5/D6 (fix-enroll-pending-code-partial-write-idempotency / fix-enroll-stable-binding-identity-key) add a second typed-error branch to respondEnrollError (raw Postgres 23505 -> retryable 503, defense-in-depth alongside the existing connector_instance_busy mapping), a fault-injection hook (maybeEnrollPhaseFault) mirroring the file's existing deviceIngestPhaseFaultHook seam so the D5/D6 oracles can inject exact partial-write/race failure points deterministically, and an explicit consumed-code-replay rejection (respondIfConsumedCodeReplay) so a declined D2 resume can never fall through to performFirstEnrollment and create an orphaned, unclaimable device. The consumed-code handling was extracted into its own function specifically to keep the route handler's own complexity flat; the residual file-level mass is the extra typed-error branch and the fault-injection seam, both load-bearing for the live 500/23505 counterexamples this closes.

server/stores/device-exporter-store.ts.reason: decouple-device-enrollment-from-ingest-writer-admission adds rotateDeviceCredential to both the SQLite and Postgres store backends (the store is a two-backend union, so a new durable primitive necessarily lands twice). Each revokes all non-revoked credentials for the device and inserts exactly one fresh credential; the Postgres variant wraps revoke+insert in withPostgresTransaction so concurrent rotations serialize on the revoke's row locks and exactly one active credential remains. D6 (fix-enroll-stable-binding-identity-key, +1) adds resolveOrCreateEnrollmentDevice to both backends: atomically resolves an existing orphaned partial-write device for a (owner, connector, binding) or creates a fresh one, serialized on Postgres by a pg_advisory_xact_lock keyed on the binding (proven load-bearing by a mutation test: removing the lock makes four independent Postgres oracles fail deterministically) and on SQLite by the single-writer connection (no explicit lock needed, documented in the method itself). D7 (fix-enroll-source-kind-identity-gap, +2) qualifies advisoryEnrollmentBindingKey and both resolveOrCreateEnrollmentDevice orphan queries by sourceKind (an added parameter plus an added SQL predicate on each of the two backends' lookup queries), closing a live cross-kind adoption gap where a local_device orphan could be adopted by a browser_collector enrollment sharing the same owner/connector/binding. Proven load-bearing by a mutation test: removing the source_kind predicate from the Postgres orphan query makes the new D7 adversarial oracle fail deterministically (3/3 runs). This is the minimum surface for the credential-rotation, identity-resolution, and source-kind-isolation guarantees and cannot be reduced without dropping one backend or the qualifier.

server/auth.js.reason: D4 (fix-enroll-writer-fence-residual-coupling): gates registerConnector's derived-column repair backfill (postgresBackfillRecordSortPositionsForManifest / backfillSqliteRecordSemanticTimesForManifest) behind the same backfillRetrievalIndexes flag that already guards retrieval-index backfill, closing a live counterexample where enroll still entered the ingest writer-admission fence via this unconditional call. Tried three shapes: (1) a single nested if/else-if duplicating the Postgres-backend check (+5 mass), (2) two sequential top-level ifs sharing one cached postgresBackend check (+3, this version), (3) one combined if/else with an inner conditional on the fenced sub-call (+4, worse than (2) because the extra nesting level costs more than the duplicate branch). (2) is the minimum: the manifest-cache invalidation is unconditional and unfenced (must run every call) while the repair backfill is fenced and conditional (must be skippable), so at least one extra branch relative to the pre-fix code is unavoidable to express two different flag-gated behaviors sharing one backend check. Correctness (closing the live 503/hang counterexample) over a lower number here.
